edges.mechanism: Soy protein supplements co-ingested with levothyroxine reduced its absorption in case reports. A crossover PK study of 60 mg isoflavones taken at the same time showed no change in Cmax/AUC.
edges.evidence: Case report, PK crossover (n=12), systematic and narrative reviews; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Thyroid peroxidase inhibition. 16 mg soy phytoestrogens raised progression to overt hypothyroidism (rate ratio 3.6), but a 66 mg dose did not.
edges.evidence: Two crossover RCTs with conflicting results; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Iodine deficiency greatly increases soy isoflavones' antithyroid (TPO-inhibiting) effect.
edges.evidence: Animal and human review evidence; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Iodine sufficiency protects against the goitrogenic effect of soy isoflavones.
edges.evidence: Review of animal and human data; low certainty

edges.mechanism: True physiological change, not an assay artifact: soy raises TSH slightly (+0.248 mIU/L) without changing fT3/fT4. Genistein 54 mg/d for 3 years had no effect.
edges.evidence: MA of 18 RCTs; 3-year RCT; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Genistein, an ER agonist, cancelled tamoxifen's inhibition of ER+ MCF-7 tumor growth in mice. S-equol did not change tamoxifen PK in humans.
edges.evidence: Mouse xenograft studies; human PK with equol only; no clinical outcome data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Dietary genistein reversed letrozole's inhibition of aromatase-expressing tumor growth in mice in a dose-dependent way. S-equol did not change anastrozole/letrozole/exemestane PK.
edges.evidence: Mouse xenograft; human PK with equol only; narrative review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Weak estrogenic/ER-beta agonist activity. Animal MA showed mixed tumor effects. Cohorts of dietary soy show lower recurrence (HR 0.74), but supplement safety in survivors is not established.
edges.evidence: Animal MA, observational MAs, regulator-linked review; low certainty

edges.with: long-term high-dose use with intact uterus
edges.mechanism: Soy isoflavone tablets at 150 mg/d for 5 years raised endometrial hyperplasia (3.37% vs 0%). Pure genistein at 54 mg/d did not change endometrial thickness up to 3 years.
edges.evidence: Single 5-year RCT plus MA of estrogenicity (no ET effect); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Subtherapeutic INR with soy milk in one case (possible-probable causality). The proposed mechanism is altered transport/metabolism. Genistein did not activate haemostatic markers.
edges.evidence: Single case report involving soy food, not genistein; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Genistein noncompetitively inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 only at micromolar levels above usual plasma levels. A red clover isoflavone supplement did not change CYP1A2/2C9/2D6/3A4 probe PK. Soy may induce CYP3A via PXR in models.
edges.evidence: In vitro and human probe-drug study; interaction unlikely to be clinically relevant

edges.mechanism: Genistein lowers fasting glucose (-4 to -6 mg/dL) and HOMA-IR, which may add to glucose-lowering drugs.
Genistein lowered SBP by 8.32 mmHg in an MA and lowered BP in metabolic syndrome, so it may add to antihypertensive drugs.
edges.evidence: MA of 21 RCTs with high heterogeneity; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Hypothesized CYP24 inhibition raising vitamin D was not confirmed: genistein 90 mg/d added nothing to calcium plus D3 for 25(OH)D, PTH or bone markers. D3 plus calcium was background therapy in the genistein bone trials.
edges.evidence: RCT (n=150) and bone RCT co-intervention; no interaction

edges.mechanism: Isoflavone exposure adds up across soy, red clover and combination products. BfR notes that EFSA's safety conclusions do not cover all supplement use.
edges.evidence: Regulatory review, combination-product RCT, PK study; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: A gut-microbial metabotype (1/3 to 1/2 of people) that modifies adipose gene-expression responses to high-genistein isoflavone supplements.
edges.evidence: Crossover RCT with transcriptomics plus review; exploratory

edges.mechanism: HDL-cholesterol response to isoflavones (genistein:daidzein 2:1) differed by ER-beta-cx genotype (AA only).
edges.evidence: Single crossover RCT subgroup analysis; exploratory

edges.mechanism: Genistein lowers resorption markers (CTX, pyridinolines) and raises bone ALP/osteocalcin. These are true changes that affect interpretation of markers during osteoporosis care.
edges.evidence: RCTs and MA of 73 RCTs; moderate certainty
